name: Rekem
title: Midianite King Killed by Israel
summary: Rekem was one of the five kings of Midian who were killed by the Israelites at the Lord's command through Moses. He is also mentioned as a descendant of Caleb in the tribe of Judah in 1 Chronicles, but he is best known as one of the Midianite kings who fell in the war against Israel. The city of Rekem in the territory of the tribe of Benjamin may have been named after him or a namesake.

keyEvents.title: The War Against Midian
keyEvents.description: The Lord commanded Moses to wage war against the Midianites, who had led Israel into sin at Peor. Israel sent a thousand men from each tribe to fight.

keyEvents.title: The Five Midianite Kings Are Killed
keyEvents.description: Rekem was killed along with the other four Midianite kings—Evi, Zur, Hur, and Reba—in Israel's war against Midian.

keyEvents.title: Balaam is killed in the same war
keyEvents.description: In addition to the five kings, the prophet Balaam son of Beor was also put to death by the sword in this war against Midian.

keyEvents.title: Moses recalls the victory over the Midianites
keyEvents.description: Joshua mentions the victory over the five Midianite kings, including Rekem, as one of God's great deeds for Israel.

keyEvents.title: Rekem as a descendant of Caleb
keyEvents.description: In Judah's genealogy, another Rekem is mentioned as the son of Hebron and father of Shammai, in the line of Caleb.
